paragraphs.source_en: Moreover, since the Higgs ocean has no effect on anything moving with constant velocity, it does not pick out one observational vantage point as somehow being special, as the aether did. Instead, even with a Higgs ocean, all constant velocity observers remain on a completely equal footing, and hence a Higgs ocean does not conflict with special relativity. Of course, these observations do not prove that Higgs fields exist; instead, they show that despite certain similarities to the aether, Higgs fields are not in conflict with any theory or experiment. If there is an ocean of Higgs field, though, it should yield other con sequences that will be experimentally testable within the next few years. As a primary example, just as electromagnetic fields are composed of pho tons, Higgs fields are composed of particles that, not surprisingly, are called Higgs particles.
